provenance.orgName: London. Augustinian priory of St Bartholomew, Smithfield.
provenance.p: On fol. 2v an inscription of s. xv: 'Orate pro animabus m. Johannis Lorde et Ursule uxoris eius Simonis Briggeman Marione uxoris eius et omnium benefactorum eorundem cum quorum bonis iste liber comparatus fuit et datus hanc ecclesie per media Willemi Taylard' (inscription repeated on 119v).

That the priory of St Bartholomew the Great was intended by 'haec ecclesia' is provided by two added lists of benefactors to the priory, including the known patron Sir John Popham (c. 1395--1463) and two priors of St. Bartholomew's, Reynold (Reginald) Collier (d. 1471) and Richard Pulter (d. 1480) (fol. 120v). Among the benefactors named on fol. 121r are 'Walteri Taylard pro edificacione capelle' and 'm. Johannis Lord pro hoc processionale'.

The manuscript had formerly been owned by Thomas Woodstock (1355--1397), duke of Gloucester, son of Edward III: inscription on fol. 2r (almost completely effaced), '. . . est de la chapelle Thomas fitz au Roy, Duc de Gloucr achete de Sr Henry Wynchestre'. The chapel would have been his personal chapel rather than his collegiate church at Pleshey castle (q.v.) since this book must have been among those confiscated at his attainder and subsequently sold, to have passed to St Bartholomew's not very much later.

history.provenance: Sir Henry Wynchester, from whom purchased by Thomas of Woodstock (1355--1397), duke of Gloucester.
Confiscated and sold after Woodstock's attainder for treason. Acquired by William Taylard and friends for presentation to the Augustinian priory of St Bartholomew the Great, London, Smithfield.
Inscriptions: 'Chambirleyne' (fol. 1v, s. xv ex); 'Thomas Brudenell' (fol. 1r, s. xvi in).
Robert Harley (1661--1724), 1st earl of Oxford and Mortimer, politician.
Edward Harley (1689--1741), 2nd earl of Oxford and Mortimer, book collector and patron of the arts.
Henrietta Cavendish Harley (1694--1755), countess of Oxford and Mortimer, née Holles, patron of architecture.
Margaret Cavendish Bentinck (1715--1785), duchess of Portland, née Harley, patron of arts and sciences, by whom with her mother the Harleian library was sold to the nation in 1753.
